alerts.title: Russell Reconstitution Week
alerts.text: Annual Russell index reconstitution takes effect June 27. Small-cap additions to the Russell 2000 typically see 5-10% post-addition bid from passive fund buying. Watch for reconstitution-driven momentum in names near the cutoff.

intro: 🟢 SMALL-CAP RENAISSANCE — Russell 2000 at 2,961 (+0.76%), outperforming S&P 500 for the first time in years. Fed funds at 3.75% = massive tailwind for floating-rate debt-heavy small caps. This special edition scans the Russell 2000 universe for 10 A+ momentum & breakout setups across semis, biotech, industrials, materials, and clean energy.
strategy: We target the 3 strongest small-cap themes of June 2026: (1) AI infrastructure buildout — AEHR benefits from semiconductor testing demand surge; (2) Biotech innovation cycle — TGTX (Briumvi), TNGX (synthetic lethality), CELC (precision oncology) ride FDA approvals and pipeline catalysts; (3) Industrial renaissance — defense, nuclear (SMR), and specialty materials (LXFR) benefit from CHIPS Act + IRA spending wave + rate cuts.
regime_prose: Regime score 0.35 — classified RISK-ON. VIX at 16.78 (sub-20, 2nd session). S&P 500 at 7,500 above both 50-DMA and 200-DMA. Russell 2000 outperforming large-caps as rate cuts accelerate small-cap earnings recovery. Dollar weak (DXY ~98) supporting multinational small-caps with export exposure. Credit spreads normalizing. The regime strongly favors risk-seeking strategies: Momentum 50%, Breakout 35%, Pullback 15%.

pedagogy.title: Why Small Caps Now?
pedagogy.content: Small-cap stocks (market cap $300M–$5B) are outperforming large-caps in 2026 for the first time in years. Three catalysts drive this rotation: (1) Rate cuts — small caps rely heavily on floating-rate debt, and the Fed at 3.75% dramatically reduces interest expense; (2) Valuation gap — Russell 2000 EV/EBIT is near multi-year lows vs Russell 1000; (3) Russell reconstitution — annual index rebalancing (June 27) forces passive funds to buy new additions, creating predictable momentum. The key is quality over speculation: cash-generative firms with high margins, not speculative biotech shells.

macro_calendar.note: Manufacturing vs services split key for industrials
Rate path signals; small-cap tailwind if dovish
Hot print = rate cut delay risk
Fund managers chase winners into quarter-end

macro_thesis: The small-cap rotation is structural, not tactical. Three forces converge: (1) Rate relief — with Fed funds at 3.75% and more cuts expected, the Russell 2000's floating-rate debt burden drops dramatically. Small-cap EPS growth is accelerating as interest expense declines. (2) Fiscal tailwinds — CHIPS Act, IRA, and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act disproportionately benefit domestic small-cap industrials and clean energy. (3) Valuation reset — after years of mega-cap dominance, the Russell 2000 trades at a historic valuation discount. Quality small caps with cash flow generation and margin expansion are the sweet spot. We avoid speculative biotech shells and unprofitable tech — this scan focuses on quality momentum.

setups.name: Aehr Test Systems
setups.description: Semiconductor wafer-level test & burn-in systems — AI chip testing demand surge
setups.thesis: Aehr Test Systems is the purest small-cap play on the AI semiconductor testing boom. The company's FOX-XP and FOX-NP systems are critical for wafer-level burn-in testing of SiC (silicon carbide) and GaN (gallium nitride) chips — the power semiconductors driving EV, AI data center, and 5G infrastructure. Revenue grew 993% over the past year as every major chipmaker races to expand capacity. The stock hit an all-time high of $126.62 on June 15, then pulled back to $110 — creating a textbook momentum pullback entry at the 10-day EMA.
confirmations: All-time high $126.62 on June 15 — strong trend with higher highs and higher lows
Revenue +993% YoY driven by SiC/GaN chip testing demand from AI infrastructure buildout
Pullback from ATH to 10-day EMA = classic momentum re-entry zone
Sector leadership: SMH +3.2% this week, semiconductor testing is the bottleneck play
invalidations: Break below $97 (20-day SMA) invalidates the momentum structure
Customer concentration risk: top 3 customers = 70%+ of revenue
Valuation stretched after 10x run — vulnerable to any earnings miss
Broad semiconductor correction (SOX below 200-DMA) would drag AEHR regardless of fundamentals

setups.name: TG Therapeutics
setups.thesis: TG Therapeutics is executing a textbook biotech commercialization story with Briumvi (ublituximab), its anti-CD20 antibody for relapsing multiple sclerosis. Briumvi is gaining rapid market share against Ocrevus (Roche), with Q1 2026 revenue beating estimates and full-year guidance raised. The 52-week range is $25.28–$49.31, and the stock is consolidating just below its 52-week high — a classic breakout setup. The MS treatment market is $30B+ and Briumvi's differentiated subcutaneous formulation gives it a structural advantage.
confirmations: Briumvi revenue guidance raised — accelerating commercial traction
Trading near 52-week high ($49.31) with ascending base pattern
MS market is $30B+ and growing — Briumvi gaining share vs Ocrevus
Strong institutional accumulation: 14 new institutional positions in Q1 2026
invalidations: Break below $40.50 (50-day SMA) shifts bias to neutral
Single-product risk: 90%+ revenue from Briumvi
Competitive threat: Roche subcutaneous Ocrevus formulation in late-stage trials
Biotech sector rotation out of healthcare into cyclicals would pressure XBI names

setups.name: Tango Therapeutics
setups.description: Precision oncology — synthetic lethality platform targeting tumor suppressors
setups.thesis: Tango Therapeutics is surging on its synthetic lethality oncology platform, with the stock up 253% YTD and 46.8% in the last week alone. Wall Street analysts are hiking price targets aggressively. The company's lead program targets STK11-mutant NSCLC (non-small cell lung cancer), a large underserved population. The 7x gain over the past year reflects pipeline de-risking through clinical data readouts. The breakout above $25 on massive volume confirms institutional accumulation.
confirmations: Stock up 253% YTD and +46.8% last week — explosive momentum confirmed by volume
Wall Street hiking price targets post clinical data (multiple analyst upgrades June 2026)
Synthetic lethality platform addresses $15B+ oncology TAM with first-mover advantage
Volume 3x average on the breakout above $25 — institutional accumulation signal
invalidations: Pre-revenue biotech — clinical trial failure would cause 50%+ drawdown
Extended after 253% YTD — vulnerable to profit-taking and mean reversion
Break below $22 (prior resistance-turned-support) negates the breakout thesis
Biotech funding environment: if rates reverse higher, speculative biotech suffers first

setups.name: Celcuity
setups.description: Precision medicine diagnostics — CELsignia companion diagnostics for oncology
setups.thesis: Celcuity's CELsignia diagnostic platform identifies cancer patients most likely to respond to targeted therapies — precision oncology's holy grail. The stock surged 1,116% over the past year from $7 to $88 on strong clinical data and FDA progress. The all-time high of $144.98 was hit May 4, 2026. The current consolidation near $88 (38% below ATH) represents a potential higher-low in the uptrend if the $74 support holds. Key catalyst: Phase 2 data readout expected Q3 2026.
confirmations: 1,116% 1-year return reflects genuine clinical de-risking, not speculation
CELsignia platform has FDA breakthrough therapy designation
Consolidating 38% below ATH ($144.98) — higher-low setup if $74 holds
Precision oncology companion diagnostics = $8B market growing 15% CAGR
invalidations: Break below $74 (200-day SMA) would signal trend reversal, not consolidation
Pre-revenue stage — any clinical setback is existential
Already up 1,116% YoY — extreme valuation risk on any disappointment
Cash runway critical: watch for dilutive offering if trial timelines extend

setups.name: SPX Technologies
setups.description: Specialty HVAC & detection equipment — infrastructure modernization beneficiary
setups.thesis: SPX Technologies is a quality compounder benefiting from the US infrastructure modernization wave. The company makes HVAC systems, gas detection equipment, and power transformers — all in structural demand as data centers, EV charging, and grid modernization drive spending. Revenue grew 15.1% CAGR over 5 years, with EPS growing 23.6% CAGR. Recent earnings showed incremental margins expanding, indicating operating leverage kicking in. The stock is in a clean momentum channel above its 20-day and 50-day SMAs.
confirmations: Revenue 15.1% CAGR (5Y) with accelerating EPS growth at 23.6% CAGR
Expanding margins: incremental sales are extremely profitable (operating leverage)
CHIPS Act + IRA spending = multi-year demand cycle for HVAC, transformers, detection
One-month return +14.3% with above-average volume — institutional participation
invalidations: Market cap ~$12B = upper boundary of mid-cap, not pure small-cap
Break below $220 (50-day SMA) shifts momentum bias to neutral
Infrastructure spending could decelerate if fiscal policy reverses
Valuation at 4.4x P/S is above historical average for industrials

setups.name: Luxfer Holdings
setups.description: Specialty gas cylinders & advanced materials — defense, healthcare, clean energy
setups.thesis: Luxfer is a UK-headquartered specialty materials company (NYSE-listed) making high-pressure gas cylinders, magnesium alloys, and carbon fiber composites for defense, healthcare (oxygen cylinders), and clean energy (hydrogen storage). At $515M market cap and $19/share, it's a genuine small-cap with 49.7% 1-year returns and improving fundamentals. The company benefits from three secular trends: hydrogen economy (cylinder demand), defense spending (military-grade materials), and healthcare infrastructure. The pullback to the 20-day SMA provides a lower-risk entry.
confirmations: +49.7% 1-year return with improving revenue trend and margin expansion
Hydrogen storage exposure: high-pressure composite cylinders for H2 infrastructure
Defense spending tailwind: military-grade magnesium and composite materials
Market cap $515M = genuine small-cap with room for re-rating on earnings beats
invalidations: UK-headquartered = GBP/USD currency risk on earnings translation
Break below $16.80 (prior support and 50-day SMA) negates the pullback thesis
Niche market with limited analyst coverage (only 3 analysts) = low liquidity risk
Hydrogen economy timeline uncertainty: commercial H2 adoption slower than expected

setups.name: NuScale Power
setups.description: Small modular nuclear reactors — the only NRC-approved SMR design
setups.thesis: NuScale Power holds the only NRC-approved small modular reactor (SMR) design in the United States, giving it a massive first-mover advantage in the nuclear renaissance. Data center power demand is driving unprecedented interest in nuclear — Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have all announced nuclear power agreements. The analyst consensus target of $15.92 implies 35% upside. Short interest is declining as bears unwind, and institutional ownership is increasing. The $11–$12 range offers a technical entry near the ascending 50-day SMA.
confirmations: Only NRC-approved SMR design = regulatory moat no competitor can replicate quickly
Data center nuclear demand: hyperscalers signing nuclear PPAs at record pace
Analyst target $15.92 = 35% upside from current levels
Short covering in play: declining short interest as bearish thesis weakens
invalidations: Pre-revenue company with no commercial reactor deployed yet
Commercialization timeline risk: first reactor not expected until 2029+
Break below $9.80 (ascending trendline support) invalidates the momentum channel
Nuclear regulatory/political risk: any safety incident globally resets sentiment

setups.name: Archer Aviation
setups.description: Electric vertical takeoff & landing (eVTOL) aircraft — urban air mobility
setups.thesis: Archer Aviation is the leading US eVTOL company with 112% analyst target upside ($11.83 consensus). The company is ramping production of its Midnight aircraft, with UAE operations and FAA type certification as near-term catalysts. Institutional ownership at 63% signals smart-money conviction. The 52-week range of $4.80–$14.62 suggests significant upside if production milestones are met. At $5.58, the stock is near the bottom of its range, offering an asymmetric risk/reward. Volume has picked up +3.35% on the session with above-average participation.
confirmations: Analyst consensus target $11.83 = 112% upside from current price
Institutional ownership 63% = smart money backing the thesis
UAE operations launch + FAA type certification = dual near-term catalysts
Trading near 52-week low ($4.80) = asymmetric downside vs upside potential
invalidations: Pre-revenue with massive cash burn — dilution risk is real
Break below $4.70 (52-week low support) = new lows territory, exit immediately
eVTOL competitors (Joby, Lilium) may reach certification faster
FAA certification delays are the norm, not the exception, in aerospace

setups.name: Opendoor Technologies
setups.description: iBuyer real estate platform — instant home transactions at scale
setups.thesis: Opendoor is the contrarian play in this scan. The iBuyer platform took massive losses in 2022–2023 during the rate hike cycle but is now recovering as rates decline. At $4.47, the stock is priced for failure, yet institutional ownership sits at 63%, suggesting insiders see a path to profitability. The 3.75% Fed funds rate is the most favorable rate environment for housing since 2022. The company processes $10B+ in annual home transactions, and each 25bp rate cut directly increases home buying activity. The pullback to the 20-day SMA offers a defined-risk entry with a hard stop at $3.80.
confirmations: Rate cuts directly benefit housing: each 25bp cut = measurable increase in home transactions
Institutional ownership 63% despite bearish analyst consensus = smart money divergence
Fed at 3.75% is the best rate environment for iBuyers since 2022
Company processes $10B+ annual volume — operational leverage kicks in as volume recovers
invalidations: Analyst consensus target $4.38 is BELOW current price = bearish street view
iBuyer model has never proven profitable at scale through a full cycle
Break below $3.80 = new 52-week low territory, thesis invalidated
Hot Core PCE print (June 27) would delay rate cuts and hurt housing directly

setups.name: iShares Russell 2000 ETF
setups.description: Broad small-cap ETF — Russell 2000 index exposure for portfolio-level beta
setups.thesis: IWM is the portfolio-level play on the small-cap rotation thesis without single-stock binary risk. The Russell 2000 is outperforming the S&P 500 for the first time in years, driven by rate cuts, fiscal tailwinds, and a valuation reset. The ETF provides exposure to 2,000 small-cap names diversified across sectors. The ascending trend above both 50-day and 200-day SMAs confirms the structural rotation. Russell reconstitution (June 27) creates a short-term catalyst as passive funds rebalance.
confirmations: Russell 2000 outperforming S&P 500 YTD = confirmed rotation to small-caps
Fed at 3.75% = massive tailwind for small-cap floating-rate debt
Above both 50-DMA and 200-DMA in clean ascending channel
Russell reconstitution June 27 = forced passive buying catalyst
invalidations: IWM contains many unprofitable companies = higher beta on risk-off days
Break below $278 (200-day SMA) would signal end of the small-cap rotation
Hot inflation data could reverse rate-cut expectations and crush small-caps
Small-cap outperformance windows historically last 12-18 months — timing risk

diversification.tickers: AEHR, TGTX, TNGX, CELC, SPXC, SMR, ACHR, OPEN

thematic.rationale: Semiconductor testing demand surge from AI chip production ramp
FDA approvals, pipeline catalysts, precision oncology revolution
CHIPS Act + IRA spending, defense modernization, infrastructure
Nuclear renaissance driven by data center power demand
Asymmetric risk/reward with defined catalysts and hard stops
Broad Russell 2000 exposure for rotation play without stock-picking risk

correlation_matrix.note: Excellent decorrelation across themes. Biotech cluster (TGTX-TNGX-CELC) is the highest intra-group correlation at 0.65-0.72, offset by zero/negative correlation with industrials (SPXC, LXFR) and real estate (OPEN). IWM provides natural diversification as an ETF.

disclaimer_extra: This is a special thematic edition focused on small-cap stocks ($300M–$12B market cap). Small caps are inherently more volatile and less liquid than large caps. Position sizing should be reduced accordingly. Several setups (TNGX, CELC, ACHR, OPEN) are pre-revenue or early-revenue companies with elevated binary risk. Never allocate more than 2-3% of portfolio to any single small-cap position.
